case_title: Rakesh & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Anr.
neutral_facts: The accused were implicated in a case where a First Information Report (FIR) was lodged against them and two others for an offence punishable under Section 364 of the Indian Penal Code. The investigating officer submitted a final report stating that no case was made out against the accused and that they were falsely implicated. The Magistrate accepted the final report but directed that the case be proceeded with as a complaint case. Statements under Sections 200 and 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were recorded, and the accused were summoned for trial. The accused challenged the Magistrate's decision to proceed with the case after accepting the final report, and the High Court answered the question in the affirmative, allowing the Magistrate to take cognizance of the case on a protest petition. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision, stating that the Magistrate is not bound by the final report and can take cognizance of the case on a protest petition if it is justified.
